title: Car Fleet
summary: Count how many groups of cars arrive at a destination when faster cars get stuck behind slower ones.

tests.explain: The cars at 10 and 8 each need 1 time unit, so they arrive together. The car at 5 needs 7, and the car at 3 would need only 3 but is stuck behind the car at 5, so those two form one fleet. The car at 0 needs 12 and never catches anyone. Three fleets.
A single car is a single fleet.
The car behind is faster at each step, but cars cannot pass, so all of them reach the target together as one fleet.

hints: Cars cannot pass each other. A car that would arrive earlier than the car in front of it ends up stuck behind that car and arrives together with it. Which quantity decides whether that happens?
Process cars from the closest to the target to the farthest. For each car compute its time to arrive if nothing blocked it: (target - position) / speed.

Sort by position descending. Keep a stack of fleet arrival times. If the current car's time is greater than the time on top of the stack, it never catches that fleet and starts a new one (push). If it is less than or equal, it merges into that fleet (do nothing). The answer is the stack size.

complexity.time: O(n log n): dominated by sorting the cars by position
complexity.space: O(n) for the sorted list and the stack
